_doc: Bands each metric should fall in, with the reason. A band is a statement about the genre (retro dungeon synth: Fief, Erang, Old Tower, early Mortiis), not about taste. Weights say how much a miss costs in the total. Melodic bands marked 'Calibrated' were checked with exemplars.py against public-domain tunes written out in tools/music/exemplars/; run `eval.py calibrate reference/` on real recordings to replace the acoustic ones. Per-mood overrides sit under 'moods'.

mode_fit.why: Modal: pitches stay inside one diatonic/modal collection per 20 s window.

pc_entropy.why: A tonal centre: seven classes used unevenly. Uniform twelve would be 3.58.

mel_step_ratio.why: Mostly stepwise. Calibrated: real tunes 0.27 (an arpeggiated shanty) to 0.64 (chant, Greensleeves).

mel_leap_ratio.why: Some leaps of a fourth or fifth (organum, horn calls), not many.

mel_large_leap_ratio.why: Leaps beyond a fifth are rare.

mel_range_phrase.why: Narrow-ish range. Calibrated: real tunes span 7 (Scarborough Fair) to 15 (Greensleeves) semitones a phrase.

mel_distinct_phrase.why: A tune, not a trill: real tunes use 5 to 10 pitches a phrase.

mel_density.why: Slow: half a note to three notes a second while the melody plays.

motif_recurrence.why: Motifs stated and repeated within a piece (180 s memory); a random walk scores 0.05-0.15.

bar_repetition.why: Statement and repeat (A A'), ostinato-like melody bars; never 1.0, which is a loop.

long_novelty.why: Endless: windows minutes apart share few figures, so it never becomes a fixed loop.

grid_alignment.why: A pulse the layers share, not free drift.

harmonic_rhythm_s.why: A harmony lasts one to four bars.

dissonance_time.why: Open fifths and triads; seconds and tritones are colour, not texture.

active_parts.why: Layered: a drone or pad under a line, usually more.

layer_changes_min.why: Layers enter and leave: orchestration is the variation engine. Too many is flicker.

silence_ratio.why: Nothing sounding at all should be rare (a breath between pieces).

counter_repeat.why: The counter is a line: it moves, held tones are tied rather than re-struck.

counter_above_mel.why: The counter stays under the tune.

melody_prominence.why: The tune sits on top of the mix: at least as loud as the loudest accompanying layer, not a soloist over silence.

drone_vs_melody.why: The drone is felt, under everything.

lufs.why: Background music at a sane level, leaving room for the UI sounds.

tilt_db_oct.why: Dark and warm: the spectrum falls steeply above the low mids.

hf6_share.why: Little above 6 kHz: low-passed, cassette-like highs.

low_share.why: A floor of drone and pad; not a bass-heavy mix either.

side_ratio.why: A stereo image from reverb and chorus, not mono, not phasey.

envelope_roughness.why: Smooth swells and soft attacks: the RMS envelope changes slowly.

swell_db.why: Slow volume swells over tens of seconds, not a flat wall.

hole_ratio.why: No dead digital silence: tails and room fill the gaps.

spike_db.why: No sudden loud moments: the loudest second stays within 8 dB of the typical one.

audio_repeat.why: The repetition survives into what is heard, through the reverb.

render_speed.why: Cheap enough to play beside the game: the offline render runs at least eight times faster than real time on one core (live play then costs under an eighth of it).

max_voices.why: No pile-up of voices that never finish.

wet_db.why: Lots of reverb: the hall's return within 8 dB of the dry signal, never above it. The genre's records are washed in it.

scene_response_s.why: A new place gets new music soon: the next piece starts within a phrase or two of the change (journeys only).

scene_response_max_s.why: Even the slowest change of scene is answered within twenty seconds.
